card.band: 20 h. CPU fine-tuning is slow (mostly single-threaded), so schedule choices decide the result. A frontier agent beats the baseline in some trials by fine-tuning, but few tune the preprocessing and augmentation for noise shift. A weaker model overfits or breaks the model format.
card.cheat: Training on the evaluation books is blocked because they are not shipped. The evaluation uses an unseen split, and the model file size is capped so a lookup of text is not possible.
card.grading: Hidden line images from books and prints never seen in training are run through the delivered model. The score is the character error rate, normalized between the shipped stock-model baseline (0) and our reference (1) and clamped. Output is run deterministically with a fixed seed.
card.reference: Our fine-tuned LSTM from make training plus tuned binarization and deskew, run on the same split. The CER is measured by us and not copied from any source.
card.task: /app ships tesstrain, the Tesseract tools, a stock model and a training split of line images (images plus text from GT4HistOCR subcorpora). The agent trains and tunes the pipeline (preprocessing, network spec, augmentation, schedule, dictionary) within the CPU budget. It then delivers a traineddata file and an optional preprocessing script.

source_notes: GT4HistOCR: 313,173 line image + text pairs, 4.0 GB tar, German Fraktur and Early Modern Latin; q:"A total of 313,173 ground truth lines are provided." Subcorpora use different transcription guidelines (train per subcorpus). tesstrain: MAX_ITERATIONS default 10000, TARGET_ERROR_RATE default 0.01, RATIO_TRAIN 0.90; README gives no CER numbers or timing. OOD: hold out a whole subcorpus/book/print (but transcription-convention mismatch adds noise, so prefer hold-out of books within a subcorpus) or degrade images with unseen noise/blur. INFERRED run time on 8 CPUs: fine-tuning on 5-10k lines 30-120 min (Tesseract LSTM training is mostly single-threaded, unverified); CER eval on 1k lines ~1-2 min. Levers: preprocessing, net spec, augmentation, lang model/dictionary, training schedule. Distinct from public corpus.
source_version: Baseline: stock Tesseract model via START_MODEL (README example uses deu_latf) with no fine-tuning, or a classical template/pixel-feature classifier -> Reference: fine-tuned LSTM from make training on in-domain lines, or tuned preprocessing (binarization, deskew) + stock model

spike_plan.kill_if: stock CER is already within 1 point of the best fine-tune (no headroom), or training cannot be made deterministic
spike_plan.pass_if: fine-tuned CER is at least 30% lower than stock on the held-out book, and a run of 2000 iterations finishes in under 60 minutes on 8 cores
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, install Tesseract 5.3+ with training tools and Leptonica; clone tesstrain at 405346a.
Download one GT4HistOCR subcorpus (not the full 4 GB) and split it into a train and a held-out book set; keep the held-out book out of training.
Run make training with a short MAX_ITERATIONS (about 2000) on 8 cores and time it; record iterations per minute.
Compute CER of the stock model and of the fine-tuned model on the held-out book with the same binarization.
Repeat once with a fixed seed to check determinism of the traineddata and CER.
Check the stock model's CER on the held-out book to see whether there is headroom.

v1.summary: The seed is real and sealable: tesstrain (Apache-2.0, pinned) and GT4HistOCR (CC BY 4.0, 313,173 lines) are both public and licence-clean, and the hidden split is not shipped. The main risk is headroom: public GT4HistOCR-trained Fraktur models (frak2021, UB Mannheim) may make the stock baseline strong, so the spike must measure stock CER on a held-out book before committing to a 20 h tier.

v2.note: Licences of the data (CC BY 4.0) and the tool (Apache) are confirmed. However, the reference is just the documented 'make training' recipe plus tuned binarization. A weaker model running the same Makefile target would get most of the normalised gain, so the 0.20 frontier lead is unlikely, and the task is effectively one lever. Headroom is unknown: public frak2021/UB Mannheim models were trained on GT4HistOCR-style data and may already cover the hidden books, which would also contaminate the OOD split. No CER or timing numbers were found.
